scope: Theorem 9.1 (Cyclic compatibility of the error) of the manuscript “A Counterexample to Kurosh’s Division-Ring Problem” (preprints/A-Counterexample-to-Kuroshs-Division-Ring-Problem-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 201 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9195b0a83fc63370), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 28. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let Z(s1, s2) be a pair of formal series in two free letters, with constant term diag(P1, . . . , Pm). Suppose that the fixed-root Schur expressions Si,h, for every block i and every root label h, vanish in every degree below ℓ, where ℓ ≥ 1. By transfer, their degree-ℓ coefficients are scalar on their root spaces; write [sω ]Si,h = ei,h,ωπi,h, |ω| = ℓ. For each word the scalar tuple at block i belongs to its active space. For every cyclic orbit O of words of length ℓ and every c ∈ G, ∑︂ ω∈O m ∑︂ i=1 ∑︂ h∈Ii ci,hei,h,ω = 0. (9.1) The orbit sum runs over distinct words, including when a word has a nontrivial rotational stabilizer.
